rows.note: This is the all-purpose verb for an object rolling, and it also covers pressing or levelling something with a roller.

example.english: I watched the ball roll across the floor.
example.jyutping: ngo5 tai2 zyu6 go3 bo1 hai2 dei6 haa6 luk1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for a rolled-up object such as paper, cloth, wool, or a bundle.

example.english: Don't get this roll of paper wet.
example.jyutping: ni1 gyun2 zi2 m4 hou2 zing2 sap1

rows.note: Use this for a small bread roll served with a meal, rather than a filled wrap.

example.english: Breakfast comes with a bread roll and scrambled eggs.
example.jyutping: zou2 caan1 jau5 caan1 baau1 tung4 caau2 daan6

rows.note: Use 捲 for rolling paper or material into a cylinder and for winding it around something; 包住 is often more natural for ordinary wrapping.

example.english: I roll the paper into a tube.
example.jyutping: ngo5 zoeng1 zoeng1 zi2 gyun2 sing4 jat1 tung4

rows.note: Use this for flatbread or a similar food wrapped around a filling.

example.english: I want a chicken roll for lunch.
example.traditional: 我想要一份雞肉卷餅做午餐。
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 jiu3 jat1 fan6 gai1 juk6 gyun2 beng2 zou6 ng5 caan1

rows.note: Use this colloquial departure sense when “roll” means to leave or get going, as in 走啦.

example.jyutping: sik6 jyun4 faan6 ngo5 dei6 zau2 laa1

rows.note: Use 流 for water or liquid moving steadily onward or trickling down a surface.

example.english: You can watch the rainwater roll down the wall.
example.traditional: 你可以睇住啲雨水沿住牆流落去。
example.jyutping: nei5 ho2 ji5 tai2 zyu6 di1 jyu5 seoi2 jyun4 zyu6 coeng4 lau4 lok6 heoi3

rows.note: Use this for an official register or formal list of names or records.

example.jyutping: cing2 hai2 ming4 caak3 soeng6 cim1 meng4
